A: A Troubleshooting/Advice: specific problem or symptom -> necessary setting -> known constraints -> one answerable question. Assigned hypothetical inquiry is allowed; do not steal the historical author's symptoms or measurements.
B: B Finding/Benchmark/Result: most notable reported result -> minimum necessary evidence -> why it matters -> implication or discussion if useful. Do not convert to "should I use this model?". Preserve incomparable conditions and uncertainty.
C: C Opinion/Debate/Trade-off: defensible viewpoint or tension -> evidence/example -> meaningful trade-off -> optional dissent invitation. Distinguish interpretation from fact; do not manufacture a radical conclusion.
D: D Showcase/Release/Resource: what it is/can do -> useful capability -> target users -> limitations -> optional experience/discussion invitation. Third-party curator, not creator; archived releases are not newly released today.
